terms.comment: To draw a sword, gladium stringere (Cic. Phil. 2.21, Lewis & Short).
Almost only in the poets (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a wooden practice sword, a foil; a toy sword
terms.comment: The staff with which soldiers and gladiators practised; a gladiator was given one on his discharge (Lewis & Short). Its use for a child’s wooden sword is ours.

phrases.latin: fulgentem gladium ē lacūnārī saetā equīnā aptum dēmittī jussit
phrases.english: he had a gleaming sword let down from the ceiling, hanging by a single horsehair

phrases.latin: additus ab īnsolente Gallō ponderī gladius, audītaque intoleranda Rōmānīs vōx, Vae victīs
phrases.english: the arrogant Gaul threw his sword on the weights too, and the Romans heard words they could not bear: ‘Woe to the beaten!’
